title: Document the one-command task sync workflow in both projects' skills
outcome: Document the one-command task sync workflow in both projects' skills
acceptance: Engram and TermAl gain the same portable task-data-sync skill telling the sync owner to run `engram task-sync sync` after one-time enrollment: no Git commands, inventory roots, baselines, fingerprints, extra approval or new gate

The skill gives the simple workflow: export local planning, fetch and reconcile incoming changes, import them and publish by fast-forward; after resolving a reported conflict or held/refused import, repeat the original command with the same options rather than force-push, rebase or blindly retry

The skill states the practical limits: one sync writer per local project data folder, public-remote disclosure and `--no-push` when review is needed, live claims/delivery/private scratch never transfer, committed task deletions may retire ids, and memories use the explicit export/import route with `--include-memories`

Markdown-only changes pass the focused launcher link check and receive the required Codex+Claude review pair in each repository; Engram and TermAl coordinators record the matching ownership and landing
disposal_reason: Duplicate filed concurrently (Kimi 16:56Z, Fable 16:53Z) for Greg's request in Asistant #2089. Engram's portable usage skill already exists as docs/skills/engram-use/SKILL.md, so the change belongs there, not in a second skill. Kimi's content points (one writer per folder, claims and scratch don't transfer, deletions retire ids, memories stay explicit) are folded into w-17be55703464's acceptance. TermAl's mirror is tracked by Termal::Fable2 in TermAl.
